results.title: Netherlands vs Japan team news and predicted lineups | Squawka | EN
highlights:
Ronald Koeman had to make a late change to his Netherlands squad for the World Cup. Jurrien Timber had been a doubt ahead of the tournament following an injury, but featured in the Champions League final. However, the Dutch FA have decided that it wouldn’t be medically responsible for Timber to take part at the World Cup. He has been replaced in the squad by Lutsharel Geertruida.
[...]
Unlike a lot of other nations, Japan only had one pre-tournament friendly, against Iceland. But their starting XI seems pretty set, and Japan appear ready to deal with the absense of Kaoru Mitoma who will miss the World Cup through injury. Takefusa Kubo and Junya Ito are set to play in the supportive attacking roles in Japan’s 3-4-2-1 formation. Ayase Ueda will lead the line after his phenomenal club season.
[...]
Ritsu Doan has emerged as a favoured for the right-wing-back role, taking it ahead of Yukinari Sugawara. Keito Nakamura is set to start on the left, though Yuto Nagatomo provides years of experience as a backup. In the middle, Wataru Endo had to withdraw from the squad on the eve of the tournament due to injury, subsequently retiring from international football. Daichi Kamada is set to start in Endo’s stead, with Leeds United midfielder Ao Tanaka likely to partner him.
[...]
Japan do have a lot of centre-back options for the World Cup, and the back three could be a number of different combinations. Maya Yoshida played against Iceland but is not in Japan’s World Cup squad, and will likely be replaced in the starting lineup by Tsuyoshi Watanabe. Ko Itakura and Takehiro Tomiyasu are the favourites to join him in defence. Zion Suzuki has made the No.1 spot his own after fine performances for club and country in 2025-26.
[...]
Japan (3-4-2-1): Suzuki; Tomiyasu, Itakura, Watanabe; Doan, Endo, Tanaka, Nakamura; Kubo, J Ito; Ueda.

# Japan captain Wataru Endo out of World Cup with foot injury

Sign up now: Get the biggest sports news in your inbox

Japan's Wataru Endo signing autographs for fans during an open training session in Nashville on June 8.

PHOTO: Getty Images via AFP

Published Jun 12, 2026, 01:26 AM

Updated Jun 12, 2026, 01:36 AM

Listen

NASHVILLE – Japan captain Wataru Endo has withdrawn from his country’s World Cup squad due to a foot injury, the Japan Football Association said on June 11.

The 33-year-old Liverpool midfielder had a left foot surgery in late February and made his return in Japan’s send-off game against Iceland on May 31 in Tokyo, but came off at half time.

He had been training separately from the rest of the Japan squad, making a partial return to the full-team training in Nashville on June 10. KYODO NEWS

results.title: Football: Kamada leads Endo tributes as Japan look to surmount late blow
highlights:
Football: Kamada leads Endo tributes as Japan look to surmount late blow
[...]
NASHVILLE, Tennessee - Japan players were rocked by the news Thursday that injured captain Wataru Endo had been ruled out of the World Cup on its opening day.
[...]
Crystal Palace midfielder Daichi Kamada, who played with Endo as a youngster while on loan at Sint-Truiden in the 2018-19 season before appearing with him in the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, lamented the departure of the influential skipper.
[...]
"I have lots of things going through my mind," Kamada said regarding the 33-year-old. "We've been having lots of chats, not so much about his injury but on football and our team. It was a surprise for me (and a shock), especially as I have known him since I was 18."
[...]
At the same time, the 29-year-old was mindful of the manager and the medical team who had to face up to the cruel reality and act for the sake of collective success.
[...]
's a tough
[...]
for a player to be in, but conversely it's not easy for the ones making the decision either," he said.
[...]
Bayern Munich defender Hiroki Ito had two seasons at Stuttgart playing under Endo's captaincy and lauded his quality.
[...]
Trusted by popular manager Jurgen Klopp in his first season at Liverpool, Endo saw his playing time nosedive in the past two seasons under the sacked Arne Slot and was expected to be an option off the bench for Hajime Moriyasu at the World Cup.
[...]
Endo's starting berth has recently been taken by Mainz star Kaishu Sano, who also excels in midfield duels, while Leeds' Ao Tanaka arrived at the tournament on the back of a strong Premier League debut campaign.
[...]
"It's really disappointing (to lose Endo) after the members were confirmed. I've been seeing his progress with rehabs and he was telling me he was gradually getting there," Tanaka said. "But we have to shift our focus when that's needed. We know what we have to do."
[...]

results.title: Japan Withdraws Injured Midfielder Endo, Calls Up Machino
highlights:
# Japan Withdraws Injured Midfielder Endo, Calls Up Machino
[...]
Japan Withdraws Injured Midfielder Endo, Calls Up Machino
[...]
# Japan Withdraws Injured Midfielder Endo, Calls Up Machino
[...]
Manager Hajime Moriyasu faces criticism for including veteran before withdrawal, replacing with forward Shuji Machino for World Cup
[...]
[Sports Chosun Reporter Noh Joo-hwan]Ultimately, it was an overreach by Japan national football team manager Hajime Moriyasu. Veteran midfielder Endo Wataru, Liverpool, 33 years old, withdrew from the World Cup squad due to injury. With the tournament opening imminent, the decision was made that he could no longer contribute to the team's strength. A forward was called up as a replacement.
[...]
The Japan Football Association announced on the 12th that central midfielder Endo had no choice but to withdraw from the World Cup squad due to injury. As a replacement, they selected forward Shuji Machino, Mönchengladbach. Endo, 33 years old, underwent surgery on a fractured foot in February and made efforts to recover in time for the World Cup schedule. As a result, he missed almost the entire second half of Liverpool's 2025–2026 season. Despite having no confidence in his form and physical condition, on the 15th of last month, Manager Moriyasu included Endo in the final squad. This decision drew criticism as being overreaching.
[...]
Captain Endo, who joined the national team, also played 45 minutes in a recent friendly match against Iceland. After facing setbacks in his recovery, Endo conducted individual training for the past week at Japan's base camp located in Nashville, United States.
[...]
Machino, who unexpectedly joined the squad, was born in 1999 and currently plays as a forward for Borussia Mönchengladbach in the German Bundesliga. Standing at 1m85, he excels at post-play, holding onto the ball and linking up plays at the front, and also possesses a powerful mid-range shot. Based on his performance at J-League's Shonan Bellmare, he joined German club Holstein Kiel in 2023 and scored 11 goals in his first season, later transferring to Mönchengladbach. He plays alongside South Korean national team member Jens Castrop. He was also part of the 2022 Qatar World Cup squad and will now step onto the World Cup stage for the second time in his career.
[...]
Japan will face the Netherlands, Sweden, and Tunisia in the group stage of this World Cup. Their goal for this tournament is to advance to at least the quarterfinals. Japan's first group match will be against the Netherlands, scheduled to be held on the 15th. Reporter Noh Joo-hwan nogoon@sportschosun.com

results.title: Football: Seasoned veterans, senior members to buttress high-flying Japan
highlights:
Football: Seasoned veterans, senior members to buttress high-flying Japan
[...]
But their veteran players showed no sign of contentment with the recent successes at their base camp in Nashville on Wednesday as they went through their paces ahead of Japan's Group F opener on Sunday against the Netherlands, another traditional powerhouse.
[...]
"I fully understand friendlies and the first
[...]
of the World Cup are totally different animals," said 34-year-old defender Shogo Taniguchi. "We'll strive together and adjust until the very last moment in analyzing our opponents."
[...]
Making a Japan record fifth straight World Cup squad, 39-year-old Yuto Nagatomo echoed that sentiment by using the group-stage exit at the 2014 tournament in Brazil under Alberto Zaccheroni as a bitter point of reference.
[...]
Hajime Moriyasu-managed Japan have been publicly talking about their dream of going all the way and 25-year-old fullback Yukinari Sugawara, set for his World Cup debut, believes the team's unique setup will stand them in good stead.
[...]
In addition to Maya Yoshida and Takumi Minamino, the two active senior players accompanying the squad despite knowing they are not registered to play at the tournament, former Japan stars Makoto Hasebe, Shunsuke Nakamura and others are on hand to provide valuable insights as coaching staff.
[...]
"I think this is the biggest sporting event on the planet...From here on, tournament debutants could feel something different to normal as matchdays approach," Sugawara said. "That's when getting ourselves into the best shape, calling on everything possible including the seasoned senior members, becomes key."
[...]
"How far can we go? Hopefully all the way," captain Virgil van Dijk said. "We know how difficult it will be, but our full focus will be on Japan first and foremost."
[...]
"Now it's down to us to make sure we start winning games. (On) Sunday there is a very difficult match waiting for us against (a) very good Japan, disciplined with lots of quality, and it's something we look forward to."
[...]
